pass_a_gloss: And this too let us know, that the thing said about Abel, taken off by the man-killing and unjust Cain, fits all of whom the blood was poured out unjustly. For the saying, voice of blood of your brother shouts toward me out of the earth, let us consider to be said also about each of the witnesses, of whom the voice of the blood shouts toward God from the earth. And perhaps also, just as by the valuable blood, that of Jesus, we were purchased, Jesus having taken the name above every name, so by the valuable blood of the witnesses some will be purchased, and they themselves being raised higher beyond what they would have been raised, having become just but not having borne witness. For it has reason, the calling of the death in witness a raising on high in a special sense, as is plain from the saying: if I am raised high out of the earth, I will drag all toward myself. Let us then also ourselves give glory, having raised high by our own death God, since the witnessing one by his own death will give glory to God; which thing also itself we have learned from John, having said: and these things he said, signifying by what sort of death he will give glory to God.
pass_b_english: Let us also know this: that what is said of Abel, killed by the murderous and unjust Cain, fits all whose blood has been shed unjustly. For let us consider that “the voice of your brother's blood cries out to me from the earth” (Genesis 4:10) is said also of each of the martyrs, the voice of whose blood cries out to God from the earth. And perhaps, just as we were bought with the “precious blood” (1 Peter 1:19) of Jesus, when Jesus received “the name that is above every name” (Philippians 2:9), so some will be bought with the “precious blood” of the martyrs; and the martyrs themselves will be exalted more than they would have been exalted had they become righteous but not borne witness.

For there is good reason why death in martyrdom is called, in a special sense, an exaltation, as is clear from the words, “If I am lifted up from the earth, I will draw all to myself” (John 12:32). Let us too, then, glorify God, exalting him by our own death, since the martyr “will glorify God” by his own “death”. This too we have learned from John, who said, “He said this signifying by what death he would glorify God” (John 21:19).
